Bible Lesson 1
Topic: The Valley of Dry Bones
Bible Text: Ezekiel 37:1-10
Memory Verse: Ezekiel 37:10 (KJV)
“So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon
their feet, an exceeding great army.”

Opening Questions:
 • Have you ever seen a skeleton or the bones of a dead animal? Can you imagine seeing bones
 scattered all over the ground?
 • Have you ever seen a dry stick or a dry leaf? Can it grow again by itself? Why or why not?
 • Do you think God can bring something that seems dead back to life?

The Story of the Dry Bones
In the bible text, God showed the Prophet Ezekiel a valley full of dry bones. The bones were scattered
everywhere. There was no life in them. They could not move, stand, speak, or do anything at all. It was
indeed a hopeless situation. Then God told Ezekiel to speak His words to the bones. As Ezekiel obeyed,
something unbelievable and amazing happened. And that's what we want to learn today; how God can bring
life into dry and hopeless situations in your life.
What Dry bones represent
When prayer becomes tiring, studying the bible becomes boring, you feel shy to tell others about Jesus,
you no longer enjoy being in God's presence, you easily fall into sin. All of these could be a sign of dryness
in our lives. Dryness can also affect other areas of our lives not just our spiritual life. Areas such as our
school work and academics, our relationships with others, our attitudes and behaviours, our peace and
happiness.

You Need the Breath of God
When Ezekiel prophesied unto the bones as commanded by God, the bones came together but there was
still no life in them until God breathed into them. In the same way, we need God’s Holy Spirit to bring new
life into every area of our lives. The bones came alive, stood up and became a very great Army. That's what
God wants to do with anything that is dead in our lives. God wants to restore: our walk with Him, prayer
life, peace, love for Him, joy of salvation, academics, relationship with others, bible study life, evangelism
etc. God wants to bring all these areas of our lives back to life through His breath.

God is Able to Restore You
Sometimes we lose hope because of: Failure, Fear, Sickness, Sin, Family problems or Disappointments. But
God has power to restore everything that has become weak or broken. He can restore our love for Him,
joy of salvation, peace, good behavior and our passion for serving Him. God is able to get you back on the
track and keep you moving again for Him just like He did to the dry bones. You can rise up again to become
part of His great army.

Discussion Questions:
 • Do you think there are areas of your life that are dead and dry and need the breath of God?
 What are those areas of your life?
 • What made the dry bones come together and live again?
 • Why do we need God’s Holy Spirit in our daily lives?

Prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You because You are the God who brings life to dry bones. Please breathe
new life into my heart. Restore my love for You, my prayer life, my joy, and everything that has become
dry in my life. Help me to trust You and to stand strong as part of Your great army. In Jesus' name, Amen.

Bible Lesson 2
Topic: Standing as Jesus' Army
Bible Text: Ezekiel 37:10, Ephesians 6:10–18
Memory Verse: Ephesians 6:11 “Put on the whole armor of God, that ye may be able to stand against the
wiles of the devil”.

Opening Questions:
 • Have you ever seen soldiers or an army? How do they dress when they are preparing for battle?
 • Why do you think soldiers wear special uniforms and protective equipment?
 • As Christians, who is our real enemy?

The Christian Army
A Christian army is one who has been saved from sin, follows Jesus, and is ready to live for Him every day.
You remember the dry bones in the valley. When Ezekiel prophesied into them and God sent His breath
into them, they became an exceeding great army. That’s who God want you to be- a great army.

Why is the Armor of God Needed?
Someone going into battle needs to be protected, just like an earthly military soldier who is going for battle
needs protective wears such as a helmet, boots, a shield, and a sword. The soldier could not possibly go to
war without the right equipment; he would definitely be a target and most likely be wounded if not killed.
In the same way, a Christian needs protection too from the dangers that comes from the enemy; the devil.
If you’ll be part of the great army of God, you need to always put on these protective and defensive wears
to protect your heart, your mind, your thoughts from the arrows that constantly comes from Satan.

What Is the Amour of God?
The armor of God is not visible, not something we wear on our bodies rather they are attributes that God
has given to you (as a Christian) to protect your heart and mind from every attack the devil launches at
you. There are six of them. Let’s take a look at each of them and how they are to be used.
 • The Belt of Truth: This is the first thing you’ve got to have and wear as a Jesus army. You must
 always love and speak the truth. Remember the belt holds everything in place. This will help you to
 be grounded. So, tighten your belt of truth so that the devil will not get you.
 • The Breastplate of Righteousness: Do you know if a soldier probably have bruises and some cuts
 on the arms and legs, that won’t stop him from still fighting but it’s difficult to survive a wound to
 the heart. That’s why breastplates are essential. As followers of Christ, you have to be righteous
 to fight the battle. This means doing what is right according to God’s word. By wearing this, you are
 protecting your spiritual heart from the damage that sin can cause. “Thy word have I hid in mine
 heart, that I might not sin against thee.’ Psalm 119:11
 • The Gospel Shoes of Peace: This is the third piece of the armor. It won’t be nice to go bare footed
 to war, you’ve got to put on footwear to protect your feet. The shoe prepares you to tell the good
 news of peace. You have to be ready to share the story of how Jesus came to save us by dying for
 us on the cross.
 • The Shield of Faith: The shield protects a soldier from arrows. Having the shield of faith means
 trusting God when life is difficult. When Satan sends fear, doubt, or temptation, our faith in God
 protects us and helps us remain strong.
 • The Helmet of Salvation: This is equally important because it protects the head. This talks about
 our salvation. We need to receive Christ as our personal Lord and saviour. Salvation reminds us that
 Jesus has forgiven our sins and made us God's children. Knowing we belong to Jesus protects our
 minds from the devil's lies and gives us confidence to stand firm.

 14

• The Sword of the Spirit: This represents the word of God. This is the only armor used for both
 defense and attack. When we know God’s word, believe it, and speak it, we can resist the devil, just
 as Jesus did. Having God’s word in your heart and on your lips keeps the devil running.

Putting on the whole Armour
Just as soldiers put on their uniforms before going into battle, Christians should put on God’s armor every
day. Each day, choose to: speak the truth, do what is right, be ready to share the good news, trust God
completely. Remember that you belong to Jesus, so read, memorize, study and obey God’s word.
When we put on the whole armour of God, we can stand strong and faithfully serve Him wherever we are.

Discussion Questions
 • Where do you need to stand firm for Jesus? – in school, at church, at home, on the playground etc.
 • Which of the armour is missing in your life?
 • How can we help each other as Jesus ‘Army, seeing that an army stands together?

Prayer: Dear Jesus, help me to put on the whole armour of God every day. Fill me with truth, righteousness,
faith, peace, salvation, and Your word. Make me strong and stand firm in faith in Jesus’ name, Amen.

CHILDREN SEMINARS
Are You Saved?
What Is Salvation And Why Is It Important?

The Angel that announced the conception and the birth of Jesus, said "And she shall bring forth a son, and
thou shalt call his name Jesus for he shall save his people from their sins" Matt 1:21.
So Salvation means deliverance from our sin. The Bible says in Rom 3:23 "For all have sinned and have come
short of the glory of God". Because of the sin of the first man on earth (Adam), we all became sinners. Sin
became a part of our DNA. No one needs to teach a child to sin before he sins. You lie to cover up your
mistakes because of this nature of sin. You take things that were not given to you without permission, you
fight over things that are not meaningful, you are greedy or jealous because of this sinful nature. You may
not know why you are doing these, but you find yourself doing them. Even when you know these things are
bad, you try to stop but you can't help yourself. You find yourself doing it again and again.

This is the reason you need Salvation, because you cannot save yourself from this sinful nature, and that
is the reason why Jesus was sent to the earth to save us.
Previously in the Old Testament, when the people sinned, God made a way out for them by asking them to
sacrifice animals like the goat, lamb, oxen or even doves for the remission of their sins. Because without
the shedding of blood there is no remission of sin. You can imagine how our churches will look like if we had
to sacrifice the blood of animals and sprinkle it every time we sinned. Our churches will smell like an
abattoir because of the blood of animals that are killed.

So God made a way out for us by sending us his Son Jesus, who never sinned. He became the Lamb that
was sacrificed for the sins of the world. He qualified to be the ultimate sacrifice for our sins because he
had the nature of God, the body of a man and he willingly offered himself to take the punishment for us.
Because "the wages of sin is death." He died the most gruesome death, the highest punishment for the
worst sinner so that he can save the worst sinner.

What Do We Need to Do to Be Saved?
The Bible says "that if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe in your heart that God has
raised him from the dead, you shall be saved" Rom 10:9.

You may wonder that it is that simple? Just like that? Yes, it is that simple. "For with the heart man
believes unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation." But before you believe
with your heart and confess with your mouth, you need to repent from your sins. This means that you need
to feel sorry about the bad things you have done before. You are not making excuses for them, but you are
sorry about lying, stealing (taking things that don't belong to you without permission), being angry, fighting,
being jealous, being disobedient etc. Be sorry that you have done them before and decide that with God
helping you, you will not do them again. Acts 3:19 says, "Repent, then, and turn to God, so that your sins
may be wiped out, that times of refreshing may come from the Lord."

So, to be saved, you have to repent of your sins, believe that Jesus has paid the price for your sins, and
confess with your mouth what you believe in your heart. When you do these, you may not feel any
difference. And you will wonder whether you have become a changed person or not. If you have received
Jesus into your heart and confessed him with your mouth in all sincerity, even when you don't feel like
anything has changed, please still hold on to the belief that you are saved. Your status has changed even
when you don't feel it. "But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God,
even to them that believe on his name" John 1:12.

 21

Even when you find yourself doing things you have promised not to do again, it does not mean you are no
longer saved. What you need to do is to continue reading the Bible daily and praying for God's help to
overcome every besetting sin in your life. There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in
Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. (Rom 8:1) Don't dwell on your feelings but
continue to believe with your heart that Jesus has saved you and you continue to build a relationship with
him through reading his words and praying daily, fellowshipping (attending fellowship) and telling others
about Jesus, you will become aware of God's presence in your life.

Conclusion
You don't need to keep going out for altar calls every time you have sinned. But know you are still saved
but you need the help of the Holy spirit to overcome sin in your life. When you keep reading the words of
God daily, it washes you and helps you to know what is right and what is wrong. You also pray for daily help
to overcome sin and temptation. Don't avoid fellowship. It is fellowship that helps you to learn new things
in the Lord. Then make sure to tell others about Christ. All these will help you to continue to grow in God's
will and purpose.

HOW TO HAVE AN EFFECTIVE QUIET TIME
Introduction
Have you ever struggled trying to stay in God’s presence? Have you seen praying and studying God’s word
as a heavy burden? Have you ever wondered why it is difficult for you to wake up early and spend time
alone with God? If this is you, then today’s lesson is for you.

What is Quiet Time? {Mathew 14:23}
It is a dedicated daily time that is set aside for personal prayer, bible reading and meditation to grow and
get closer with God. It is more than a routine, quiet time is meant to get you closer to God so that you can
know Him more and also to transform your heart. It is a special time between you and God which allows you
to talk to God and also for you to hear him speak with you.

Why Have a Quiet Time?
Have you ever wondered if it was actually necessary to have a quiet time especially since you regularly do
family devotion, but do you know that even Jesus has a time he stays alone to talk to God. Let’s read
Mark1:35. Therefore, Jesus is our perfect example. Again, if you want to grow in your fellowship with God
and be transformed, you need to spend time with Him every day. Also, you need to have a quiet time to
avoid temptations from the devil.
Yes, it is good to go to church, fellowship together with other Christians but spending time alone with God
makes your friendship with him grow stronger and deeper and you get to know Him better.

What to do During Quiet Time
 • Prayer: Quiet time should be time to pray to God through worship, praises, intercession and request.
 You also share things that disturbs your heart with God and so many other things.
 • Bible reading: Quiet time is a two-way communication, this means that when you speak to God, he
 will also speak to you. Reading the bible is one of the ways God can speak to you. You can read a
 chapter of the bible every day. You can start reading from the book of John or you can use a
 devotional if you have one.
 • Scripture meditation: focusing deeply on a single verse and thinking about it and how to use it in
 your everyday life. This brings about changes in your life.
 • Journaling/Jotting: This has to do with writing down what God is saying especially through His word
 or whatsoever that drops in your heart during your quiet time. You can also write your prayer
 requests and what you are trusting God to do for you.

How To Do Quiet Time
There is no rule to doing quiet time. It depends on what works for you. If one method does not work for
you, try another method until you find what works for you. However, we can follow Jesus as an example of
how He talks to God when He was on earth.
 • When should it be? Mark 1:35 gives us a clue ‘a great while before day’. This means very early in
 the morning. This is the best time to do quiet time before the day’s activities and when there is no
 noise but if this will not work for you, choose a time that will work, it could be immediately after
 school, before dinner, or even before bed time but make sure it’s the same time every day. The
 most important thing is to have a special time with God consistently.
 • Where should it be done? Still on Mark 1:35, the latter part says ‘and departed into a solitary
 place’ this means a quiet place, where there are no distractions. Therefore, look for such place to
 do your quiet time. You might need to pray and think of where you can be having it.
 • Gather things to Use: You need a bible, pen, jotter, devotional {if available}
 • Start with Prayer: Read Matthew 14:26, There are lots of things to tell God about. Start with
 thanksgiving, sing, tell God how much you love Him, tell him who He is. Another thing you must tell

 23

God is to say you are sorry for any wrong doings (John 1:9) and lastly ask. God is always willing to
 help us if we will ask in prayer. In asking, you can also pray for others (intercession).
 • Read the Bible: 1peter 2:2. If you desire to grow in your walk with God, you must read your bible.
 You can pick a chapter, read it two to three times. Look out for God’s promises, instruction, what
 you need to learn and also memorize a verse. Read Psalm 119:11
 • Meditate/Think: As you read the bible over and over, God can drop something in your heart, think
 on those things carefully
 • Write: make it a habit of jotting things, or thoughts that come to your mind. Put a date on your
 jotter and the passage you read, then write the part of the scripture that means so much to you.
 Also, write down whatever you think God is saying. This helps you to remember what God says to
 you. Habakkuk 2:2

Conclusion (2 Corinthians 3:18)
Quiet time is more than a routine, rather it helps to develop a consistent relationship with God. This
enhances our spiritual growth. If you do it as just a mere routine, it will become burdensome and boring.
But, if you do it as if you need to talk to your friend every day and become intimate with him, then it
becomes an everyday encounter that transforms you and makes you become like your friend (Jesus) indeed.

Topic: Excelling with God, Discipline, and Hard Work
Text: Daniel 1:17–20
Memory Verse: Proverbs 22:29 "Do you see someone skilled in their work? They will serve before kings;
they will not serve before obscure men."

Introduction
Sade and Bola are both children of God, they were obedient and excelling in other areas of their lives but
were very poor academically. What do you think is responsible for this?
What is Academic excellence? Academic excellence is about consistently doing your best and using the
abilities God has given you to achieve your God’s desired goal for you in life. God expects us to be diligent,
disciplined, and faithful in everything we do.

Case Study: Daniel
Daniel and his friends stood out because they feared God, remained disciplined, and worked hard. As a
result, God gave them wisdom, knowledge, and understanding beyond their peers (Daniel 1:17–20).

Keys to Academic Excellence
1. Have a Relationship with God
* Pray daily.
* Read and meditate on God's Word.
* Trust God for wisdom and understanding. Prov. 3: 5 – 6, James 1:5

2. Set Clear Academic Goals
* Be excited and driven by clear life goals / vision
* Know what grades you want to achieve.
* Set daily, weekly, and term goals.
* Review your progress regularly.

3. Develop Effective Study Habits
* Create a study timetable.
* Be a passionate reader
* Study consistently instead of cramming.
* Take notes during lessons.
* Revise regularly.
* Ask questions when you don't understand.

4. Manage Your Time Wisely
* Prioritize your studies.
* Limit unnecessary screen time and social media.
* Balance academics, rest, family time, and church activities.

5. Build Self-Discipline
* Be committed to self-development
* Avoid procrastination.
* Complete assignments on time.
* Stay focused on your goals.
* Never give up

6. Choose Good Friends- 1 Cor. 15: 33
* Friends influence your character and performance.

* Surround yourself with people who encourage learning and positive values.

7. Maintain Good Character
* Be honest during tests and examinations.
* Respect your teachers and parents.
* Accept corrections and keep improving.
Common Obstacles to Academic Excellence
* Laziness
* Procrastination
* Poor time management
* Excessive use of phones and social media
* Bad company
* Fear of failure
* Lack of self-confidence
* Examination malpractice

How to Overcome These Challenges
* Pray consistently.
* Stay disciplined.
* Develop a positive mindset.
* Seek help from teachers and parents.
* Study smart and work hard.

Discussion Questions
* What does academic excellence mean to you?
*What habits are affecting your academic performance?
* How can social media help or hinder your studies?
* What practical changes will you make after this seminar?

Practical Steps to achieving Academic Excellence
* Pray before studying.
* Read for at least one hour daily.
* Complete all assignments on time.
* Reduce unnecessary phone use.

Conclusion
Academic excellence is a journey of commitment, discipline, and dependence on God. Like Daniel, you can
stand out among your peers by living a life of integrity, working diligently, and trusting God for wisdom.

Emotional Intelligence
Biblical Emotional Intelligence for Seed of Purpose
Objective: To teach children that God created their emotions, how to name them biblically, how to pause
and invite the Holy Spirit into big feelings, and how to respond with Christlike love toward others. Psalm
139:13–14, Proverbs 4:23

Introduction: Emotional Intelligence is the God-given ability to understand and manage our feelings. The
Holy Spirit helps us to pause during big emotions and respond to others with Christlike love. Emotions are
God's design, God gave us feelings just like He gave us eyes to see and ears to hear. Joy, sadness, fear,
and anger are signals that tell us what is happening inside our hearts. Jesus while on earth, He displayed
his emotions as well.
I. Jesus felt sad (John 11:35
ii. Jesus felt angry at sin (Mark 3:5
iii. Jesus felt joy (Luke 10:21

Self-Awareness
Naming the feelings you are having, as Seed of purpose you don’t just act without self-awareness. Before
we react, we must name what we are feeling. After that, the first step is to tell God, Lord, right now I
feel angry or sad or afraid etc.

Activity: The Emotion Weather Map
Stick four weather symbols on a board: Sun (Joy), Rain (Sadness), Thunder (Anger), Fog/Wind
(Fear/Anxiety).
Have 3-4 children place a sticky note on the "weather" matching how their heart feels right now. Remind
them: "Just like God rules over the sky's weather, the Holy Spirit helps us navigate our heart's weather.

Self-Regulation
The Holy Spirit helps children to pause before reacting in anger, jealousy, or frustration.
James 1:19 Proverbs 16:32 Galatians 5:22–23:

Stop & Breathe Inhale God's Peace
 • S- Stop or Pause immediately. Take a deep breath while praying in your head: Lord, give me peace.
 • T — Think & Name, identify the Feeling you are having. Ask yourself: "What am I feeling, and why
 am I feeling this way?" (Proverbs 4:23)
 • O — Open God's Word. Filter Through Scripture Ask: "What would Jesus want me to do right now?"
 (Philippians 2:5)
 • P — Proceed with Love. Act in the Spirit, respond with the Fruit of the Spirit, (kindness, gentleness,
 and self-control) instead of striking out.

Object Lesson: A bottle of Maltina vs. A bottle of water
Materials: 1 bottle of clear water, 1 bottle of unopened Maltina drink

Demonstration:
Shake the 2 bottles. When bad things happen or someone treats us unfairly, we feel shaken up inside. If I
open this bottle right now, what happens? It explodes everywhere and hurts people around us. Now shake
the water bottle. Show that even when shaken, clear water stays calm when opened.
Lesson: "Self-control doesn't mean we never get shaken; it means through the Holy Spirit, we don't explode
on others.

7 Pillars of TACEF Seed of Purpose

The Covenant Mandate of the Seed of Purpose

"A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation" (Ps.22:30)

At TACEF, we view every child as a covenant seed, making them very special. In the vision of revival,
children are living arrows, shaped and sent out as agents of revival for their generation (Psalm 127:3–5).

This study guide outlines the principles and introduces the seven pillars designed to shape all our children
into Christ-like agents of revival for their homes, churches, communities, and nations.
The TACEF mandate emphasises that raising children must be inclusive and holistic. God's plan for growth
focuses on whole-life formation, as seen in these examples:

 • “And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man” (Luke 2:52).
 • “And the child Samuel grew on, and was in favour both with the LORD, and also with men” (1 Samuel
 2:26).
 • “And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon
 him” (Luke 2:40).

This holistic approach means a child's mind, body, spirit, character, relationships, and mission are all shaped
through a well-rounded discipleship practice. This process produces boys and girls who pray, think, speak,
work, love, and serve effectively. The ultimate goal is a child "thoroughly furnished unto all good works"
(2 Timothy 3:17).

The Seven Pillars of the Seed of Purpose
The seven pillars of the Seed of Purpose are reflected in the seven dimensions outlined in Luke 2:52:
 • Wisdom (Mental/Academic and Creative): God forms curious, diligent, and inventive minds that
 use knowledge for godly solutions.
 • Stature (Physical/Health): Since bodies are God’s temples, children learn hygiene, exercise, rest,
 and self-control.
 • Favour with God (Spiritual and Moral): New birth, purity, obedience, and godly speech produce a
 life that pleases the Lord.
 • Favour with Man (Social and Global): Children grow in love, etiquette, teamwork, courage, public
 witness, and a mission heart for all nations.

Thus the 7 Pillars of the Seed of Purpose—Spiritual, Moral, Mental/Academic, Social, Physical,
Creative, and Global—are the Bible’s own portrait of a well-formed child, seen in Jesus and echoed in
Samuel.

 Rahab could have turned them away. But she kept them safe.

 and on earth." How did she know? She had heard stories about God. How He parted the Red Sea. How He
 helped Israel win. Those stories changed her heart.

 She also asked the spies for one thing. "Please save me and my family when you take this city." The spies
 said yes. They told her, "Hang a red cord in your window. Gather your family inside. You will be safe." Rahab

deserve it. God is kind even to your classmate who is always in trouble or your neighbour who seems hard
to reach. God can forgive even the person you think will never change.

 #2. Stories About God Can Change Someone’s Life

Rahab believed because she heard stories about God. Those stories gave her faith.

Your personal stories of God matter too. When you share what God has done in your life, it could open
someone else's heart to Him. Don't be afraid to share your story.

 #3. The Red Cord Points to Jesus

That scarlet cord in Rahab's window saved her whole family.

It's a picture of Jesus. His blood saves us, just like that red cord saved Rahab and the people she loved.

No matter what someone has done, the blood of Jesus is powerful enough to save them. That's the good
news we carry.

 They had crossed the Jordan River. They had set up the memorial stones. God had rolled away their shame

 The city of Jericho was right in front of them. It had huge walls and looked very hard to defeat. But before
 the battle, something amazing happened. Joshua was near Jericho when he saw a man standing in front of
 him with a sword. Joshua asked the man, "Are you on our side or the enemy's side?"

 The man said, "Neither. I am the Captain of the Lord's army." Joshua did not argue. He fell to the ground and
 worshiped. Then he asked, "What does my Lord want to tell me?" The Captain said, "Take off your shoes. The
 ground you are standing on is holy." Holy means that place belongs completely to God, so it's different and
 special. Joshua obeyed right away.

 #1. Jesus Is the Real Commander
 This tells us something important. Jesus is the one in charge – not us. Maybe you are the leader of your group
 at school. Or maybe you are the oldest at home. It can be easy to think you are the boss. But even leaders
 need to follow Jesus. He is the real Commander. Our job is to listen to Him and obey.

 #2. Ask God First Before You Act
 After Joshua found out who the Captain was, he stopped and asked, "What does my Lord want to tell me?"
 He didn't rush into battle. He asked for instructions first.

 We should do the same. Before you make a big decision – like choosing who to be friends with or what to
 when someone is trying to fight you at school – stop and ask God. Say, "Lord, what do you want me to do?"

 God always has the best answer.

 #3. Come to God with a Humble Heart
The Captain told Joshua to take off his shoes because the ground was holy. Taking off your shoes was a sign
of respect. It meant, "I know I am before someone much greater than me." When we come to God, we should
come the same way. Not with pride. Not with a heart full of wrong things. Before you pray today, say sorry
for anything wrong.

Then come to God with a clean and humble heart. That's how He wants us to come.

So far, Israel won two battles already. Jericho fell. Ai was taken. Things were going really well. But then

A group of people called the Gibeonites were afraid of Israel. So instead of fighting, they made a plan to trick
them. They put on old torn clothes. They carried old worn shoes. They brought dry old bread. Then they went
to Joshua and said, "We came from a very far country. Please make peace with us."

Joshua looked at their old bread and worn clothes. It all seemed to match their story. So he agreed. But he
made one big mistake. He did not ask God first. Three days later, the truth came out. The Gibeonites were not
from far away. They lived right next door! It was all a trick. And Israel fell for it because they did not pray first.

 #1. Things Are Not Always What They Look Like
The Gibeonites looked like tired travellers. But they were not. It was all fake. Sometimes things can look one

is why we cannot just trust what things look like. We need to ask God to help us see the truth.

 #2. Ask God Before You Decide
Israel's big mistake was not asking God first. They used their own eyes and got it wrong.

Before you make a big choice, like who to be close friends with or whether to follow a crowd, ask God first.
Say, "Father God, is this a good idea? Is this right for me?" God always knows the truth. And He will help you if
you ask.

 #3. Slow Down and Think Carefully
The Bible tells us to walk carefully.

We should not act like a fool, but like someone who is wise. That means slowing down before you decide. Not
going along with something just because it looks good.

Ask questions. Always pray. Talk to someone you trust like a parent or a teacher. Wise people don't rush. They
think. They pray. They ask God to guide them!

Last week, we talked about how the Israelites defeated five kings because God
fought for Israel. After that win, the five kings ran away and hid in a dark cave.
Joshua found out.
But instead of stopping, he told his men to roll big stones over the cave. Then he said, "Don't stop! Keep going
after the rest of the enemies!"

The five kings were hidden. If Joshua had left them there, they could have come back and caused big trouble
later. It's the same with us. Sometimes, we try to hide or ignore our problems.

Maybe you had a fight with a friend. But you never said sorry. You just acted like it never happened. But that
problem is still there. It’s just hiding like the five kings in the cave. Later on, that problem could come back and
cause bigger trouble for you. So don't leave it or ignore it. Say sorry to your friend. Make it right.

Always remember: Hidden problems don't go away on their own.

 #2. Don't Stop Too Early

Joshua told his men, "Don't stop! Keep going!" They didn’t stop just because victory was at hand.

It's easy to quit when things feel okay for a while. Maybe you said you would read your Bible every day. You
did well for a few days. Then you stopped. Don't stop too early. Keep praying. Keep reading your Bible. Keep
doing what is right – especially when things are going well. Good habits need to keep going, not just start.

 #3. Don't Give the Devil a Chance
The Bible says, "Don't give place to the devil."

That means don't leave any open door for bad things to get in. Maybe you know that some videos you watch
make you think bad thoughts. But you keep watching them anyway. Or maybe you have friends that are a bad
influence to you. That's giving the devil a way in!

Stop watching those videos. Stop spending time with bad friends. Choose what is good. Don't give the enemy
any space in your life. God wants your whole heart, not just most of it.

Israel had been winning many battles. But the battles were not over.

A new and much bigger problem came from the north. A king named Jabin heard about
Israel. He was scared. So, he called many other kings to join him.

Their army was so big it was like the sand on the beach! They had horses, too. And big war machines called
chariots. This was the biggest fight Israel had ever faced. But God told Joshua, "Do not be afraid. I will give them
all to you tomorrow." And just like before, God kept His word. Israel won!

But God also gave a special rule. He said, burn the chariots and destroy the horses. Joshua obeyed. All of it. He
left nothing undone.

 #1. Higher Levels Bring Harder Battles

Israel kept winning. But each new battle was bigger and harder than the last. That is how life works. When you
grow, the tests get more difficult too. When you move to a higher grade at school, the work becomes harder
and the tests become longer.

That is not a bad thing. It just means you are growing. And don't be scared. Just ask God to help you with bigger
things as you grow.

 #2. Always Put Your Trust in God

God told Joshua to burn the chariots and destroy the horses. Even though they looked strong and useful. Why?
Because God did not want Israel to start trusting in horses instead of trusting in Him. It is the same with us. It
is easy to trust in our own ideas or our own strength instead of God.

Before you try to fix a big problem, stop and ask God first. Trust Him. Don’t just rely on yourself or your own
abilities.

 #3. Do All of What God Says

Joshua did not obey some of God's words. He obeyed all of them. He left nothing out. When God asks you to
do something, like say sorry to someone or stop a bad habit, don't do it halfway. Don’t say “Sorry” half-
heartedly. Do everything you need to do. Finish it.

That is real obedience. And God is pleased when we do everything He says!

The kings in Joshua were strong. Their cities were fortified with giant walls. But they all fell before God. The
Bible says Jesus is now above every power and every name in the whole world. He has already won the biggest
battle of all. He won over sin and over death.

That means nothing you face is bigger than Jesus. No fear can overcome you. No hard problem can defeat you.
No sad situation can put you down. Why? Because Jesus is above them all. And He is on your side!

Joshua 12 records wins from both Moses and Joshua. It did not say only Joshua did it all.

It gave credit to Moses too. And most of all to God. When good things happen in your life, say thank you to

Let’s continue the story of Joshua and the Israelites in the Promised Land.
After so many battles, Israel had finally taken a lot of the land. Now it was
time for Joshua to divide the land among the Israelites.

Israel had 12 tribes. Each tribe got their own portion. Their own piece of land to live and care for. The land was
different sizes for different tribes depending on how many people each tribe had. Some got more. Some got
less. But every tribe got something. But one tribe – the tribe of Levi – got no land at all.

Why? Because God said He would be their portion. God Himself was their inheritance. That means instead of
land, they got something even better: a special relationship and closeness with God forever.

 #1. Everyone has a Part to Play

Every tribe got a job. A piece of land to take care of. It’s also the place where they can serve. It is the same in
God's family. Everyone has something to do. Maybe you are good at singing. Or praying. Or being kind to new
people. Or helping clean up after an event.

All of those things matter. God gave each of us something special to use for Him. So don't say, "I have nothing
to give." You do. Just ask God to show you what it is and then use it.

 #2. Don't be Jealous for Someone Else's Part

Each tribe got a different portion of land. Some looked bigger. Some looked smaller. But every tribe had to be
happy with what God gave them and take care of it well. It can be easy to look at what someone else has and
wish it was yours. Maybe your friend gets to sing in front of everyone, and you wish you could do that too.

But God gave you your own special assignment. It might be different from other people. But it is just as
important. So be happy with what God gave you. And take care of it well!

 #3. When Everyone Does Their Part, Everyone Grows
The Bible says the body of Christ grows when every part does its job. Think of your body. Your eyes help you
see. Your legs help you walk. Your hands help you hold things. If one part stops working, the whole body suffers.

It is the same in God's family. When everyone does their part – praying, helping, sharing, serving – the whole
group gets stronger. So do your part because every part matters.

Today we are going to meet another special character in the Bible.
His name is Caleb, a friend of Joshua.
Many years ago, when Israel was preparing to enter the Promised Land, Moses sent twelve men to spy
out the land. Joshua and Caleb were among them.

Ten of the spies came back scared. They told the Israelites, "The people living there are too big and too strong. We can't
win against them!" But Caleb and his friend Joshua said something different. They were very excited to enter the
Promised Land and they told the people, "God is with us. We can do this!" Caleb trusted God. That’s why God made a
special promise to him. God told Caleb, "The land your feet walked on will be yours one day."

Caleb received that promise forty-five years ago. Now he is eighty-five years old. Israel is sharing the land. Most people
his age would ask for something easy and small. But not Caleb.
He walked up to Joshua and said, "Give me this mountain!" The mountain he wanted had giants living on it. Big strong
people called the Anakims. Hard cities with tall walls.

But Caleb still wanted to take possession of it. Why? Because God had promised it to him. And Caleb knew God would
never fail. Here’s what we can learn from Caleb’s faith:

 #1. Don't Give Up on God's Promises
 Caleb waited forty-five years. That’s a very long time! But he never stopped believing that God would fulfil His promise
 to him. Maybe you are waiting for God to answer a prayer right now and it feels like you’ve been waiting for a really long
 time. Don't give up. God does not forget His promises. Keep trusting Him. His timing is always right.

 #2. Don't Always Pick the Easy Way

Caleb did not pick the easiest land. He picked the hardest. Not because he’s confident of his own strength. It’s because
God promised it to him and Caleb knew that God would fight for him. Sometimes God asks us to do hard things. Maybe
it is standing up for what is right when your friends don't. Maybe it is being kind to someone who is not kind to you.
Don't always pick the easy way. Ask God to give you strength to do the right thing even if it’s hard.

 #3. Stay Strong on the Inside

 Caleb said, "I am just as strong now as when I was forty."
 How?
 He stayed on God’s side every day. His strength didn’t come from his own abilities. It came from the inside.
 The Bible says God can make us strong on the inside through His Spirit. It means God’s own power living inside us and
 helping us in everything we do. When you pray, read the Bible, and trust God, He makes you stronger inside. And that
 inner strength helps you face even the hardest things.

Today we meet five sisters in the Bible.
Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. They were the
daughters of a man named Zelophehad.

Many years ago, their father had died. And in those days, when a father died with no sons, the family could lose their
land. But the daughters of Zelophehad knew God had made a promise that He would give the Israelites the Promise Land.
And the sisters believed that God’s promise was for them too.

So they did something bold. They walked up to the leaders and told them, "Our father died and he had no sons. But
please give us our land too." It took real courage to stand up and ask in front of everyone.

Moses did not push them away. He asked God about their situation. And God answered, "They are right. Give them their
land." The daughters of Zelophehad received what God had promised.

 #1. It’s Okay to Ask
These sisters could have stayed quiet. They could have just accepted that they’re going to lose their land and move on.
But they didn't. They spoke up, talked to the leaders, and God said they were right. Maybe you need help at school but
you feel too shy to ask your teacher. Maybe something is bothering you at home but you don't know how to bring it up.

It's okay to ask. Just be respectful when you do. God loves it when we are brave and kind at the same time.

 #2. God Gave You Something Special
The sisters knew God gave their father a portion of land so they asked for it. God has also given every one of us something.
He gave you gifts, abilities, and a place to serve. Maybe you are good at helping people. Maybe you are good at making
others feel welcome. Maybe you are great at praying. Maybe you have talent in singing or dancing.

That's not an accident. God put that in you. And He wants you to use it.

 #3. You Have a Place in God's Family
The Bible says everyone who believes in Jesus has a place in God's family. That means God has a place for you. And you
also have something to offer. God put it in you.
And He always keeps His word.

Israel had won many battles. A lot of the land had been taken. But seven tribes
still hadn't received their land. The land was ready for the taking. God had
already given it to them. But they just hadn't gone to take possession of it.

So Joshua asked them a ‘not-so-gentle’ question. He asked them, "How long are you going to wait before you go and
take the land God gave you?" Ouch!

Good thing Joshua also gave them a plan. He said, “Send some men to walk through the land. Look at it carefully. Write
down what you see. Come back and report. Then we will divide it up.”

The men followed Joshua’s instructions. They walked through the land, wrote everything down, and came back. And
Joshua was able to give each tribe their portion. The lesson? God had already done His part. Now it was time for them
to do theirs.

 #1. Stop Waiting and Start Moving
The tribes had everything they needed. The land was right there. But they just kept waiting. Maybe it’s the same with
you. Perhaps God has already given you something – an ability, an opportunity, a chance to help someone. But you keep
putting it off. Don't wait too long. Start with one small step today.

Maybe that's saying sorry to someone you hurt. Maybe it's reading your Bible a little more. Maybe it's helping out at
church when someone asks.
God already did His part. Now it's your turn.

 #2. Make a Plan
Joshua didn't just tell the tribes to go. He gave them clear steps to follow.
That's a good lesson for us too. When God gives you something to do, think about how you're going to do it.

For example, if you want to pray more, decide when. Before school? Before bed? Pick a time and stick to it. Having a plan
makes it so much easier to actually do it.

 #3. Don't Waste Time
The Bible says we should use our time wisely because our days matter. Time is a gift from God. And like any gift, we can
use it well or waste it.

Think about how you spend your afternoons after school. Are you using that time for something good? Ask God to help
you use your time in a way that makes Him happy.

Sometimes, when we make mistakes, we feel scared that people would
be angry at us. Today’s lesson will teach us how to handle those kinds of
situations.

In Chapter 20 of the Book of Joshua, God told the Israelites to set up special places called “Cities of Refuge.”
It’s a place where someone who hurt another person by mistake could go to. The people in that city would
keep that person safe until they’re able to find out the truth of what happened.

By doing this, no one could hurt the person who made a mistake. And they could do a proper investigation to
know exactly the truth. Here’s what we can learn from this:

 #1. Learn to Listen First
In ancient Israel, if a person hurts another intentionally, there will be a punishment for them. The Cities of
Refuge are for those people who hurt or kill someone by accident so that they won’t be punished without
hearing the truth first.

We should do the same when someone makes a mistake. Don’t judge the person right away. Instead, listen to
what they have to say first. Give them a chance to explain themselves then find if what they’re saying is true.

 #2. Be Kind to People Who Made Mistakes
The Cities of Refuge were for those people who made some really big mistakes. But God didn’t want others
judging them immediately. Instead, He wanted these persons to be safe first so they could know the truth.

It means even if the person made a terrible mistake, God still wanted the people to be kind to that person and
give them a chance to talk. You can do the same. Maybe a classmate got into trouble at school. Instead of
laughing at them, you could express kindness to them and listen to what really happened.

 #3. Jesus is our Safe Refuge
The Cities of Refuge actually point to Jesus. It shows us that when we do something wrong, instead of running
away from God, we should run to Him because He is our Safe Refuge.

God won’t push us away. He listens. And when we genuinely repent, which means we say sorry and turn away
from what we did wrong, He forgives us and gives us a fresh start.

That’s a wonderful promise from the Bible. God can do more than anything we can ask or imagine. Just like

We’re almost done with the Book of Joshua. But before we move forward,
let's go back a bit during the time when Moses was still alive and before they
crossed the Jordan River to conquer the Promised Land.

On the other side of the Jordan River, the tribes of Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh had already
claimed their portion of the land. It was a blessing from the Lord. But Moses told them that even though God
already gave them their own territory, they still have to cross the Jordan River and fight side by side with the
other tribes. So, that’s exactly what they did.

They crossed the Jordan River and stood with the rest of Israel until they won every battle. When it was all over,
Joshua called the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh. He told them, "You kept every
command. You stayed with your brothers. You never gave up." Then he blessed them and sent them home with
a reminder to stay faithful to God.

 #1. Be Faithful Before God Opens the Next Door
Before the two and a half tribes could go home to their territory on the other side of the Jordan, they needed
to stay faithful to their assignment first – which was to help the other tribes conquer the Promised Land. And
they accomplished their mission. So, when the time came, Joshua sent them home. In the same way, God
wants us to be faithful to our assignment before He sends us to our next mission. It’s important that we always
do our best with the things He entrusted to us. And when we prove ourselves to be faithful, that’s when God
brings us to the next big thing.

 #2. Take Your Faith With You Wherever You Go
Joshua reminded the two and a half tribes to stay faithful to God even after they went home to the other side
of the Jordan River. In your life, you’ll go through many different situations as well. New school. New friends.
New places. Make sure you always take your faith with you. Wherever God takes you, keep praying, keep
reading your Bible and keep loving God.

Joshua told the two and a half tribes to go home to their families and carry with them all the riches they took
after the battles. He also told them to share their blessings with their brothers. When good things happen to

Long before Joshua's story ever began, there was an Israelite man who lived in
Egypt named Joseph. He was a very important person during his time and he’s
actually the second-in-command to Egypt’s King.

Because of Joseph’s unusual wisdom, the King appointed him to take care of the whole country. A lot of lives
were saved because of what Joseph did. And that’s why he was loved by so many people.

Despite all his success, before Joseph died, he asked his family and his people for a special promise. He told
them, "One day, God will bring you out of Egypt. He will take you to the land He promised us. When that
happens, please carry my bones with you." Hundreds of years later, the Israelites finally left Egypt. And they
kept their ancestors’ promise to him. They carried Joseph's bones all the way to the Promised Land God gave
them. And they buried him there, just like Joseph had asked.

 #1. Joseph Kept Believing God’s Promise
Originally, God gave His word to Abraham about the Promised Land. Abraham was Joseph’s great-great-
grandfather. So, Joseph knew that the Israelites, which were Abraham’s descendants, were not supposed to
stay in Egypt. He believed that one day God’s promise would come true. But Joseph would not be alive to see
it. So, he planned for it and told his people to take his bones to the Promised Land when God fulfils His promise
to them. We should do the same. When God gives you a promise, believe that it’s going to happen no matter
what.

 #2. Joseph Knew that Egypt Was Not His Final Home
Joseph had an amazing job and a nice life in Egypt. He could have called it home and chose to just stay there.
But deep down, he knew that his final home was the land God had promised his family. So he prepared to get
there when the time came. In the same way, this world is not our final home. God prepared a better place for
us in the future.

 #3. Jesus Will Raise His People and the Rapture
Joseph believed God’s promise so strongly that, before he died, he asked that his bones should one day be
carried to the Promised Land. His faith reminds us that death is not the end for God’s people. The Bible teaches
that when Jesus returns, believers who have died will be raised, and believers who are still alive will be caught
up together with them to meet the Lord. This event is often called the Rapture. God’s children should therefore
live ready for Jesus, trusting His promise and looking forward with hope to being with Him for ever.

This week we look back at everything we have learned about Joshua and God's
people. It’s been a whole year of studying the Book of Joshua and we learned
a lot!
Going back to what we’ve learned, we can see that anytime God was going to do something big for His people,
Joshua kept saying the same thing over and over to the Israelites: “Get ready!”

Before they crossed the Jordan River to conquer the Promised Land, Joshua told them, "Get ready. Tomorrow
the Lord will do amazing things." The Lord wanted their hearts and minds ready for what He’s about to do. He
did not just want them to ready their swords and shields. God wanted their hearts to be clean and prepared
because He’s going to do something super awesome.

 #1. Get Ready Before the Big Moment
You do not wait until the game starts to put on your shoes. You get ready first. God wanted His people prepared
before He did something big for them. Isn't that smart? Getting your heart ready means praying, saying sorry
for anything you said or you did wrong, and trusting God before the big moment even comes. That way, you
are not rushing around at the last minute.

 #2. Let God Clean Out the Old Stuff
Before the people could move forward, God wanted them to do something very important. He wanted them
to leave their old habits behind for good. It’s like cleaning out a messy closet to make room for new toys. It
might feel hard at first because you might not want to let go of old stuff. But you have to do it to make space
for something better.

 #3. Don't Hide What's Wrong

In the beginning of our study of the book of Joshua, we met a man named “Achan.” He was a troublemaker
who took something he was not supposed to take. That caused a big problem for everyone. So God punished
him. Hiding a problem does not make it go away. It just grows bigger and bigger. It is always better to tell the
truth quickly, even when it feels scary.

TACEF VISION/MANDATE
Raising an army with a vision of revival through focused discipleship, prayer and the ministry of the
Word; to groom a generation of Godly and heaven-conscious youths and adults who are conformed to
the image of Christ and to live each day to promote the purpose of God in The African Church and
advance the cause of evangelism/revival to the world at large. The fellowship is raised to be the
"repairer of the breach", "to build the old waste places" and "to raise the foundation of many
generations". (Isa 58 vs 12).

It is important to know and note that:

 1. TACEF/TACESF is not an association, society or an ordinary group, it is a heavenly calling.
 2. TACEF/TACESF is not a gathering of youths, but a gathering of God's end-time army: students
 and non-students of all age groups learning under the tutelage of the Spirit of God.
 3. TACEF has a revival mandate to The African Church and will remain committed to serving God's
 will in the Church.

Our motivation is that we strongly believe that The African Church is at the threshold of a great
revival in the dispensation of God and we are fully persuaded that the Lord is equipping the Church
for the end-time revival.

Our prayers and pursuit therefore shall continue to be the promotion of the purpose of God in The
African Church. We shall continue in prayers and the ministry of the word, as we trust the Lord for a
season of total spiritual awakening. We trust the Lord that in all of our local churches, the Word of
God will take pre-eminence and the Spirit of the Lord will dominate. We believe the Lord for a
rekindled passion for the dying souls under the grip of the evil one and a renewed pursuit of holiness
without which no man shall see the Lord.
